title: Root-free scatteredness criterion for the explicit four-coordinate finite-field family in the small-Frobenius-exponent regime
difficulty: The sufficiency argument eliminates scalar intersections through a Frobenius polynomial and proves exceptionality across infinitely many field extensions. The necessity argument constructs a Kummer curve from a root, computes its genus and excludes boundary places to force a forbidden finite-field intersection by Hasse–Weil. Both directions are one restricted criterion, not separate variants.
scope: The selected problem is the exact paired original Theorems3.2 and3.4 scatteredness/root-free criterion, treated as one composite. Retain the nonzero coefficients, gcd(I,J,n)=1 and distinct positive I,J setup of Section3; necessity is only the literal small-exponent regime max(I,J)<=n/4, while root-free sufficiency has the stated exceptional-scattered conclusion. The whole author article preserves notation and supporting local context; the later independent evasivity/indecomposability and GL non-equivalence programs are not selected additional claims. Named finite-field/Kummer genus and Hasse-Weil prerequisites remain references, without recursive reproof or formula repair.

title: Pretty good fractional revival on single orbits of diamond-decorated cycles after transcendental diagonal perturbation
difficulty: The proof develops H-cospectral spectral blocks, proves irreducibility of their relative minimal polynomials under transcendental perturbation, and uses a Galois trace criterion with simultaneous Diophantine approximation. Explicit Fourier-block matrices for diamond-decorated cycles then establish distinct traces on every orbit.
